To determine the fairest allocation among the given options, we should consider both fairness and efficiency. One of the common measures of fairness is the concept of "envy-freeness." An allocation is envy-free if no person prefers someone else's allocation to their own. Another measure is "efficiency," specifically Pareto efficiency, where no other allocation could make one person better off without making the other person worse off.

- An allocation is envy-free if each person values their own allocation at least as much as they value the allocation given to the other:
